newsitem.title: USA: JPE Inc to exit metal stamping business.
newsitem.headline: JPE Inc to exit metal stamping business.

text.p: JPE Inc said Thursday it will discontinue its metal stamping operations, which will result in second quarter charge against earnings of $2-$2.5 million.
JPE said the charge will cover disposal of assets and employee severances. It did not specify how many workers would be dismissed.

John Psarouthakis, JPE chairman, president and chief executive officer, said in a statement that a review of the metal stamping business at its Starboard Industries Inc unit determined that the business is not contributing to earnings.

"In fact, that line of business actually took resources away from our other businesses," Psarouthakis said. "By removing that distraction, we can focus on the technological strengths in our Trim Group that add value to the trim package we offer to our customers."

JPE said Starboard, located in East Tawas, Mich., will continue to use its metal and plastic co-extrusion and metal roll-forming technologies to produce exterior trim parts for automotive and light truck original equipment manufacturers.
The metal stamping business accounts for about $9 million of JPE's total annual revenues of about $280 million.
